messages:
maria: Quick check — I'm adding a client-side opt-out for telemetry/metrics in the JS SDK (quietMode = true). Question: when quietMode is enabled, do we still send User-Agent and trace propagation headers for routing/observability, or do we suppress everything? Also curious about retries/streaming: should trace headers be included for retry attempts and streaming reconnects?

lee: My instinct: UA is low-sensitivity and useful for server routing/metrics, so keep UA even in quietMode. Traces are more privacy-ish — probably suppress propagation unless user explicitly enables tracing. For retries/streaming, if trace is suppressed, don't send trace headers on retries either.

sam: +1 to preserving UA. A lot of infra uses UA to pick optimized kernels / routing. If we remove UA it breaks some routing heuristics.

jen: Agree with lee/sam. One nuance: server-side auditing still needs a way to correlate retries for SLO debugging. If we drop trace headers entirely, ensure we add an internal retry-id header that’s non-PII and only for server ops (e.g., X-RW-Retry-Id). That stays even in quietMode.

maria: Sounds reasonable. So final proposal:
- quietMode = true: suppress user-level tracing headers (traceparent/tracestate/b3) and client metrics payloads
- still send a minimal UA (e.g., "redwood-js/1.3.0"), and an internal-only retry-id for debugging.
- for streaming reconnects, same rules apply: preserve UA and retry-id, suppress trace headers.

sam: Implementation detail: for the JS SDK we already add headers in one place. I'll add a small function that returns header set based on opts.quietMode. Example:
```js
function buildHeaders(opts) {
  const headers = { 'User-Agent': `redwood-js/${PKG_VERSION}` };
  if (!opts.quietMode && globalTracing.enabled) {
    headers['traceparent'] = getTraceparent();
    // optionally tracestate
  }
  headers['x-rw-retry-id'] = opts.retryId || genId();
  return headers;
}
```

lee: That looks good. A couple of follow-ups: 1) we should document how to opt-out server-side for enterprises (e.g., via policy that strips UA as well) — add a note in the Console docs. 2) Make sure the telemetry opt-out doesn't disable essential routing — include a setting in account-level policy that disallows UA stripping unless authorized.

jen: On the server side, we need to ensure audit logs still capture retry-id and request fingerprinting without storing full traces. Ops wants the retry-id surfaced in tracing UI as an internal attribute (but not correlated with user-supplied trace IDs).

maria: Good point. I'll update the SDK PR to: 1) implement buildHeaders per sam's snippet, 2) add tests that ensure quietMode doesn't send trace headers, and 3) add Console docs note (lee can add the policy paragraph).

sam: I'll open the PR later today. PR checklist: unit tests for headers, e2e smoke that verifies streaming reconnect headers, and a changelog entry for the opt-out behavior.

dev-bot: deploy-preview 5278 for branch feature/quiet-mode is ready — preview URL: https://deploy.preview/redwood/quiet-mode (runs in sandbox) :rocket:

lee: Thanks! @maria @sam can you add a short note in the SDK README about the new header behavior (UA preserved, trace suppressed) and include the code example?

maria: Yep will do. Also tagging @ops-bot for audit log requirements.

ops-bot: Noted. Will provision a small schema change to persist x-rw-retry-id in the request index. Will not store traceparent when quietMode=true.

jen: One last thought — for native SDKs (iOS/Android/Rust) we should keep consistent semantics. I'll sync with platform owners, but leaving it as a follow-up item.

sam: Cool. I’ll file SDK issue linking mobile/rust follow-ups.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll send a short RFC in the #devex-docs channel after PR is up for sign-off.
